newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sets 1997 trade surplus target.
newsitem.headline: France sets 1997 trade surplus target.

text.p: French Foreign Trade Minister Yves Galland said on Tuesday that France had a 1997 trade surplus target of between 135 and 145 billion francs ($25.6 billion), including trade with its overseas territories.
He also told a news conference the dollar's appreciation should result in adding seven billion francs to the surplus in 1997 and 25 billion in 1998.
France earlier reported a 1996 trade surplus of 122.34 billion francs.
"For the coming year I am setting a target of 135 to 145 billion francs, including the overseas departments," Galland said.
While the dollar's rise on currency markets would hurt in the short term, it was beneficial over a lag period of 12 to 18 months, he said.
Galland welcomed the 1996 surplus as a boost for both businesses and jobs.
"For our companies it is a sign of formidable competitivity," he said.
"In the export sector we created 116,000 jobs in 1995," he said, adding this would be around 150,000 jobs for 1996.
